## Summary

Fourth @algojan backtest in the vault, and the first grounded in published research rather than hand-crafted rules: the listing explicitly follows **Chuk (2026)**, "Noise-band Intraday Momentum in Nasdaq-100 Futures" (SSRN 7609644), itself an adaptation of **Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (2024)** "Beat the Market" — the same lineage as several TradingView "noise band" scripts now circulating. Rules (from the listing):

- **Noise band:** each session, the band around the open = the average absolute move from the open at each minute of the day over the prior 60 sessions — volatility-scaled, carried across contract rolls.
- **Entry:** the first 30-minute check between 10:00–15:30 ET where price closes above the upper band **and** above VWAP (long), or below the lower band and below VWAP (short). One position per session; fills on the next tick after the signal bar closes.
- **Exit:** default mode = a 6-point trailing stop armed immediately, ratcheting tick by tick, with an optional $900 max-loss stop. Alternative modes: the paper's band/VWAP trailing stop, or a fixed ATR stop + take-profit (1×ATR / 2×ATR). Flat at 15:55 ET.
- **Sizing:** fixed contracts, default **50**, with a broker-delay setting to model fill latency and optional skip dates. Listing recommends a $10,000 minimum account.
- The headline 82.5% is a **1,000-run prop-firm simulation** on the backtest: 825 passed (82.5%), 174 rule-breached (17.4%), 1 timed out (0.1%).

## Dashboard (OCR, cross-checked vs listing)

Period **30 Oct 2021 → 30 Oct 2026** (5 years, tick fills). **Net +$138,429 = +1,384.3% · 986 trades (~0.79/session) · 46.0% WR · PF 1.78 · Sharpe 2.09 · Sortino 5.57 · Calmar 3.90 · CAGR +71.58% · max DD −18.4% · expectancy +$140.39/trade** · avg win +$693.74 / avg loss −$331.82 (ratio 2.09) · largest win +$4,814 / largest loss −$1,086 · commissions −$60,146 included in net. Tweet = OCR = listing on every shared number (+1,384%, 986, 2.09, 1.78, 18.4%, 82.5%). Internal math checks: 986 × $140.39 ≈ $138.4k ✓; 0.46 × 693.74 − 0.54 × 331.82 = $139.94 ✓; commissions ≈ $61/round-turn ≈ 50 MNQ contracts at ~$0.61/side — consistent with the 50-contract default; +1,384% on a ~$10k base matches the stated minimum. The listing also discloses a humbler "typical backtest profile" (~200 trades, ~48% WR, PF ~1.1, Sharpe ~0.94, ~53% net return at 41% max DD) alongside the showcase.

## Why it matters

- **The rule family joins the NQ session-structure cluster:** time-of-day noise around the open is the same object [[2026-10-26-onlybreakouts-market-mapping-time-grid]] maps and [[2026-11-11-propquantx-nq-gap-up-breakout]] trades — a third independent lens on "the first hours of NY define the day".
- **Skepticism gates — heavier than usual, and mostly external to the author:**
  1. **The underlying rule failed an independent out-of-sample test.** Chris Bailey ([cbailey.uk](https://cbailey.uk/trading/noise-area-intraday-momentum/), 13 Oct 2026) tested the Zarattini noise-area rule across 54 pre-registered settings each on MNQ/MES/MYM/M2K (2019–2024 development): all 54 MNQ and all 54 MES settings profitable, family-wise p = 0.005 — then on 20 months of unseen data it **lost money (−0.051R/trade on MES, 284 trades) and did worse than a long-only control (+0.003R)**. Notably, algojan's equity curve climbs straight through 2025–2026 — the same window where Bailey's MES validation failed. Same family, different instrument/config, opposite verdict: exactly the OOS question to answer before believing either.
  2. **The source paper is far more hedged than the showcase.** Chuk (2026): executable rule ≈ +$10.26/day on **one** MNQ, daily Sharpe **1.14** (vs 2.09 at 50 contracts), one index point of stop-fill slippage removes **22% of the edge**, all intervals in-sample, no live contract traded.
  3. **Leverage does the heavy lifting.** 50 fixed contracts vs the paper's 1-contract sizing; the 18.4% DD / Calmar 3.90 / +1,384% are products of that. Commissions are 30% of gross and included — good hygiene — but the 1,000-run prop sim inherits the backtest's assumptions; it is not a live pass (contrast the Topstep-fills leg in the 11-19 capture).
  4. In its favor: published lineage, open code, defaults disclosed, commissions and fill-latency modeled, worst loss < 2× average (no hidden martingale), one-position-per-session caps the overfitting surface.
- **Actionable → Inbox:** code is free and public; the cheap next step is reading it and re-running the backtest split OOS, with Bailey's failed replication and Chuk's degradation table as the benchmarks to beat.
